changes.reason: This scenario row is new and was not in the old Appendix 4 paragraph 4 table.

changes.new_text: Where not indicated as 'Not Applicable', the manufacturer shall declare whether the system will be able to avoid a collision, and the preconditions under which it will, for the scenario 'VUT crosses the straight path of the vehicle target in a partially obstructed intersection' (Annex 4, par. 4.2.5.2.19), without driver intervention in non-highway environments.
changes.reason: This scenario row is new and was not in the old Appendix 4 paragraph 4 table.

changes.new_text: Where not indicated as 'Not Applicable', the manufacturer shall declare whether the system will be able to avoid a collision, and the preconditions under which it will, for the scenario 'VUT turns across a path of an oncoming vehicle and cyclist' (Annex 4, par. 4.2.5.2.20), without driver intervention in non-highway environments.
changes.reason: This scenario row is new and was not in the old Appendix 4 paragraph 4 table.

changes.new_text: At least one extended test associated with each applicable base test shall be performed or witnessed during the approval process.
changes.reason: Extended tests are new. The old Annex 4 / 1 had no equivalent obligation.

changes.new_text: Further extended tests shall be performed or witnessed during the approval process at the request of the Type Approval Authority.
changes.reason: New TAA-request provision for further extended tests.

changes.new_text: For those extended tests that are not performed during the approval process, the manufacturer shall provide evidence of the required system behaviour in those scenarios.
changes.reason: New manufacturer evidence obligation for extended tests not performed.

changes.new_text: During the assessment according to Annex 3, the Type Approval Authority may identify scenarios of particular relevance with regard to safety risk.
changes.reason: New TAA permission.

changes.new_text: An identified scenario with particular safety relevance may replace a base or extended test scenario only if the manufacturer provides satisfactory evidence of test performance of the replaced scenario.
changes.reason: New conditional replacement permission.

changes.new_text: The rationale for replacing a base or extended test and a detailed description of the identified scenario applied shall be documented in the test report.
changes.reason: New documentation obligation tied to scenario replacement.

changes.new_text: For systems where identical initial conditions (e.g., path or positioning) of the vehicle in a given scenario may not always result in a repeatable outcome (e.g. using non-rule-based algorithms), the manufacturer shall explain this deviation to the Type Approval Authority.
changes.reason: New paragraph imposing a manufacturer explanation duty for non-repeatable systems. No old requirement in the provided base or old context covers it. Annex 4 3.1.6.2 repeat-test rules and 3.1.6.1 TAA-defined parameter combinations address different matters.

changes.new_text: For systems where identical initial conditions (e.g., path or positioning) of the vehicle in a given scenario may not always result in a repeatable outcome (e.g. using non-rule-based algorithms), the manufacturer shall agree with the Type Approval Authority on the ranges of different test parameterization that do not modify the objective of the test scenario and diverge from other requirements of this regulation.
changes.reason: Separate mandatory action: agreement with the TAA on parameterization ranges. It is distinct from the explanation step, and old 3.1.6.1 gives the TAA unilateral definition of test parameter combinations, so this is not an equivalent.

changes.new_text: In the Base Test for the VUT turning across the path of an oncoming vehicle in an intersection (4.2.5.2.13.1), the target vehicle (passenger car or motorcycle) shall approach at a speed of up to 60 km/h, depending on the declared system boundaries.
changes.reason: The old text has an identical sentence only at 4.2.5.2.14.1.2, which is the separate scenario where the VUT crosses the straight path of a vehicle target. It is flagged missing_parent_clause. In the new text the sentence sits under 4.2.5.2.13.1 for the turning scenario. The speed limit for the target is therefore a separately scoped test-procedure obligation for the turning base test. There is no base requirement equivalent, so it is added.

changes.new_text: In the base test for a longitudinally moving bicycle target ahead in lane, the test shall confirm the declared response capability of the system for a longitudinally moving target and any lateral movement navigating around the target, if applicable.
changes.reason: New base test scenario (longitudinally moving bicycle target ahead in lane, 4.2.5.2.16). The old 4.2.5.2.8.1 covers a stationary bicycle target, which is a different test scope, so this is a separately scoped test obligation. The wording is repeated but the procedure scope is new. The Type Approval Authority conducts or witnesses it under 4.2.5 for the declared operating domains.

changes.new_text: In the base test for the longitudinally moving bicycle target ahead in lane, the bicycle target shall be positioned within the driving path of the VUT facing away from the subject vehicle.
changes.reason: New test scenario 4.2.5.2.16 (longitudinally moving bicycle target ahead in lane) introduces its own positioning requirement for the target. Wording repeats the stationary bicycle test in 4.2.5.2.8.1.1, but that is a separate procedure with a different scope, so this is a distinct obligation scoped to the new moving-bicycle base test.

changes.new_text: In the base test for the longitudinally moving bicycle target ahead in lane, the VUT shall approach the impact point with the cyclist target in a straight line for at least two seconds prior to the functional part of the test.
changes.reason: Repeated wording from the stationary bicycle test (4.2.5.2.8.1.2) now applies to the newly introduced longitudinally moving bicycle target scenario (4.2.5.2.16). The new procedure scope creates a separately applicable obligation, so it is not a modification or duplicate of an old requirement.

changes.new_text: In the base test for a longitudinally moving bicycle target ahead in lane (Annex 4, 4.2.5.2.16.1), the bicycle target shall travel with a constant speed of 20 (+1/-1) km/h.
changes.reason: The clause sets a specific bicycle target speed and tolerance for the newly introduced longitudinally moving bicycle base test. The old context has no equivalent: the 15 km/h crossing bicycle speeds in 4.2.5.2.10.1.1 and 4.2.5.2.12.1.1 apply to different scenarios and have different tolerances.

changes.new_text: Annex 4 / 4.2.5 / 4.2.5.2 / 4.2.5.2.16 / 4.2.5.2.16.2 Extended testing for the longitudinally moving bicycle target ahead in lane: the test shall demonstrate that the system is not unreasonably changing the control strategy for a bicycle.
changes.reason: The clause is a new extended-test obligation for the new scenario 4.2.5.2.16 (longitudinally moving bicycle target ahead in lane). The old context has similar extended-test wording only for other scenarios (stationary pedestrian, stationary bicycle, crossing bicycle). The scenario scope differs, so this is not a relocation of any old obligation. The old requirements R-116 and R-117 are generic Appendix 4 control-strategy provisions and are not scenario-specific Annex 4 extended tests, so they are not modified by this clause.

changes.new_text: In the extended test for a longitudinally moving bicycle target ahead in lane, the test shall be executed at least with a bicycle target positioned with different offsets, up to the target being outside of the driving path of the VUT.
changes.reason: The offset variation resembles stationary bicycle 4.2.5.2.8.2.1(a). This clause belongs to the new longitudinally moving bicycle scenario (4.2.5.2.16), which has no old counterpart, so it is a separately scoped procedure.

changes.new_text: In the extended test for a longitudinally moving bicycle target ahead in lane, the test shall be executed at least with a different speed of the VUT.
changes.reason: The VUT speed variation exists in the old stationary bicycle test, but the moving bicycle scenario is new. This is a separately scoped test variation.

changes.new_text: In the extended test for a longitudinally moving bicycle target ahead in lane, the test shall be executed at least with a different speed of the bicycle target within the range of 10-25 km/h.
changes.reason: The bicycle target speed range of 10-25 km/h has no counterpart in the old text. It applies only to the new moving bicycle scenario.

changes.new_text: Base Test: the test shall confirm the declared response capability of the system for a cut-out of the lead M1 category vehicle when other vehicles are fully or partially blocking the lane.
changes.reason: New scenario 4.2.5.2.17 'Cut-out of lead vehicle with an interfering vehicle'. The old 4.2.5.2.5.1 base test covers cut-out of the lead M1 vehicle without blocking vehicles. The blocking-vehicle condition extends the test scope, so this is a separate, newly scoped test obligation and not a renumbering.

changes.new_text: In the base test for cut-out of the lead vehicle with an interfering vehicle (other vehicles fully or partially blocking the lane), the vehicle cutting out shall perform a full lane change (e.g., 3.5 m lateral displacement) into the adjacent lane to avoid the stationary vehicle target, with the measurement behind the stationary vehicle target indicating the start of the lane change and the measurement in front of the stationary vehicle target indicating the end of the lane change.
changes.reason: The wording repeats 4.2.5.2.5.1.1 (cut-out base test). It now applies to the new scenario 4.2.5.2.17 (cut-out with an interfering/blocking vehicle), a separately scoped test procedure under the new base test 4.2.5.2.17.1. The old procedure remains for its own scenario, so this is a new obligation, not a relocation.

changes.new_text: In the base test for cut-out of the lead vehicle with an interfering vehicle, the indicated TTC is defined as the TTC of the lead vehicle to the target at the moment the lead vehicle starts the lane change.
changes.reason: The wording is identical to old 4.2.5.2.5.1.2 (cut-out without interfering vehicle). It now sits under the new scenario 4.2.5.2.17 (cut-out with an interfering vehicle), so it applies to a new procedure scope. It is a separately scoped obligation, not a relocation. No base requirement (R-...) covers it.

changes.new_text: In the base test for cut-out of the lead vehicle with an interfering vehicle, the lead vehicle shall not use indicators during the lane change manoeuvre.
changes.reason: This is a separate test-procedure restriction (second sentence). It has the same wording as old 4.2.5.2.5.1.2, but it applies to the new interfering-vehicle scenario 4.2.5.2.17. No base requirement covers it.

changes.new_text: In the cut-out of lead vehicle with an interfering vehicle base test (4.2.5.2.17.1), the cutting out vehicle shall not deviate from its defined path by more than ±0.2 m.
changes.reason: The wording matches old 4.2.5.2.5.1.3, but it now sits under the new interfering-vehicle scenario 4.2.5.2.17. That is a new test procedure scope, so it creates a separately scoped obligation. The old cut-out test continues in its own scenario.

changes.new_text: In the cut-out of lead vehicle with an interfering vehicle base test (4.2.5.2.17.1), the cut-out at TTC = 3 s shall be run with VUT set speed 70 km/h, lead vehicle (M1 category) speed 50 km/h, lane change lateral acceleration of the SOV 1.5 m/s2, lane change length 44 m and radius of turning segment 130 m.
changes.reason: The parameter table is repeated from old 4.2.5.2.5.1.3, but it now applies to the new interfering-vehicle scenario. It is a separate test-parameter obligation.

changes.new_text: In the base test for cut-out of the lead vehicle with an interfering vehicle, the blocking vehicle in the adjacent lane shall drive under conditions where the VUT is prevented from changing lanes, specifically where the conditions of paragraph 6.2.4.1. are not met.
changes.reason: New blocking-vehicle set-up in the new scenario 4.2.5.2.17. The old context has no equivalent. The old cut-out test 4.2.5.2.5.1 and the 6.2.4.1 lane-change conditions are not the same obligation.

changes.new_text: During the cut-out of the lead vehicle in the interfering vehicle base test, the blocking vehicle in the adjacent lane shall, as one trajectory case, continue with the same constant speed. The shared condition is that the blocking vehicle drives so that the VUT is prevented from changing lanes (conditions of paragraph 6.2.4.1. not met).
changes.reason: Independent blocking trajectory (a). The shared blocking condition is repeated because the trajectories are split into separate cases.

changes.new_text: During the cut-out of the lead vehicle in the interfering vehicle base test, the blocking vehicle in the adjacent lane shall, as another trajectory case, brake with the same deceleration as the VUT, blocking the way of the lane change, until the VUT stops or passes the static target. The shared condition is that the blocking vehicle drives so that the VUT is prevented from changing lanes (conditions of paragraph 6.2.4.1. not met).
changes.reason: Independent blocking trajectory (b). The shared blocking condition is repeated because the trajectories are split into separate cases.

changes.new_text: Extended Testing for cut-out of the lead vehicle with an interfering vehicle: the test shall demonstrate that the system is not unreasonably changing the control strategy for a cut-out of the lead vehicle.
changes.reason: Clause 4.2.5.2.17.2 sits under the new scenario 4.2.5.2.17 (cut-out of lead vehicle with an interfering vehicle, p.80). It repeats the wording of old 4.2.5.2.5.2, but that clause applies to the separate cut-out scenario 4.2.5.2.5. The new test scope is therefore a separate, independently applicable test obligation. It is not shown to be a renumbering, and the old clause remains in the new text.

changes.new_text: In the extended test for cut-out of the lead vehicle with an interfering vehicle (blocking vehicles fully or partially blocking the lane), the test shall be executed at least with a stationary vehicle target of a different type or category, including cyclist and pedestrian (if the system is designed to drive in non-highway roads).
changes.reason: Applies to the new interfering-vehicle scenario 4.2.5.2.17.2. The similar old 4.2.5.2.5.2.1(a) covers cut-out without an interfering vehicle and had no cyclist/pedestrian target or non-highway condition. This is a separate scoped obligation.

changes.new_text: In the extended test for cut-out of the lead vehicle with an interfering vehicle, the test shall be executed at least with the cut-out occurring at less than 3 seconds TTC of the lead vehicle.
changes.reason: The old 4.2.5.2.5.2.1(b) wording is repeated, but under the new interfering-vehicle procedure scope, so it is a separate obligation.

changes.new_text: In the extended test for cut-out of the lead vehicle with an interfering vehicle, the test shall be executed at least with different speeds of the VUT and lead vehicle.
changes.reason: The old 4.2.5.2.5.2.1(c) wording is repeated, but under the new interfering-vehicle procedure scope, so it is a separate obligation.

changes.new_text: In the extended test for cut-out of the lead vehicle with an interfering vehicle, the test shall be executed at least with different lateral acceleration of the lead vehicle.
changes.reason: The old 4.2.5.2.5.2.1(d) wording is repeated, but under the new interfering-vehicle procedure scope, so it is a separate obligation.

changes.new_text: In the extended test for cut-out of the lead vehicle with an interfering vehicle, the test shall be executed at least with impassable objects.
changes.reason: This test condition has no counterpart in the old cut-out extended test list.

changes.new_text: Base Test for pedestrian target crossing into the path of the VUT during drive around manoeuvre: the test shall confirm the declared response capability of the system for a crossing pedestrian target, while another vehicle obstructs the lane of travel and the perception of the pedestrian target.
changes.reason: New scenario 4.2.5.2.18 (drive around manoeuvre) with an obstructing vehicle and obstructed perception. The old crossing-pedestrian base test (4.2.5.2.9.1) covers a plain crossing pedestrian without obstruction, so its scope differs. No old R-xxx requirement represents it, and the changed scope makes this a distinct obligation.

changes.new_text: In the Base Test for a pedestrian target crossing into the path of the VUT during drive around manoeuvre (Annex 4, 4.2.5.2.18.1), a static target shall be placed in front of the VUT with 50% overlap towards the edge of the road.
changes.reason: Test set-up for the new 4.2.5.2.18 scenario. The old 4.2.5.2.15.1.2 has the same static target placement, but it sits in a different scenario (adjacent-lane moving vehicle target, synchronised arrival). The scoped obligation is therefore new.

changes.new_text: In the Base Test for a pedestrian target crossing into the path of the VUT during drive around manoeuvre (Annex 4, 4.2.5.2.18.1), the VUT shall travel at least 30 km/h toward the static target with system-initiated manoeuvring activated.
changes.reason: Speed and activation condition for the new scenario. It is a separate procedural step from the target placement. The old 4.2.5.2.15.1.2 and 4.2.5.2.15.1.3 conditions apply to a different scenario with a moving vehicle target.

changes.new_text: In the Base Test for a pedestrian target crossing into the path of the VUT during drive around manoeuvre (Annex 4, 4.2.5.2.18.1), the VUT shall avoid collision with the target if performing a drive around manoeuvre.
changes.reason: Pass criterion for the new scenario. It is conditional on a drive around manoeuvre being performed. The old 4.2.5.2.15.1.3 requires avoiding collision with the targets in a different scenario, so equivalence is not established.

changes.new_text: In the pedestrian-crossing during drive around Base Test (Annex 4, 4.2.5.2.18.1.2), the pedestrian target shall travel in a straight line perpendicular to the VUT's direction of travel at a constant speed of 5 km/h +0/-0.4 km/h from a maximum of 1 m from the front of the static target.
changes.reason: New drive-around scenario (4.2.5.2.18). The pedestrian starts within 1 m of the static target's front, and the old 4.2.5.2.9.1.3 'starting not before the functional part of the test' wording and its separate scenario scope are absent. It is a separately scoped test-procedure obligation, not a continuation of the old crossing-pedestrian clause.

changes.new_text: In the pedestrian-crossing during drive around Base Test (Annex 4, 4.2.5.2.18.1.2), the pedestrian target's positioning shall be coordinated with the VUT so that the impact point of the pedestrian target on the front of the VUT is on the longitudinal centreline of the VUT if the VUT would remain at the speed it has when reaching the rear of the static target and does not brake.
changes.reason: The reference speed is the VUT speed on reaching the rear of the static target, rather than the prescribed test speed. No 0.2 m tolerance is stated, unlike old 4.2.5.2.9.1.3. This is a separate coordination obligation for the new scenario.

changes.new_text: Extended testing for the pedestrian target crossing into the path of the VUT during drive around manoeuvre (Annex 4, 4.2.5.2.18): the test shall demonstrate that the system is not unreasonably changing the control strategy for a crossing pedestrian target.
changes.reason: Same wording as old 4.2.5.2.9.2 (plain crossing pedestrian), but the new clause applies to a separately introduced scenario, 4.2.5.2.18 (drive around manoeuvre with an obstructing static target). The new procedure scope creates a new extended-test obligation rather than a relocation. R-116/R-117 are the general control-strategy and demonstration duties in Appendix 4 and do not cover this scenario-specific test.

changes.new_text: In the extended test for the pedestrian target crossing into the path of the VUT during drive around manoeuvre (4.2.5.2.18.2), the test shall be executed at least with a static and pedestrian target of a different type and/or size.
changes.reason: Old 4.2.5.2.9.2.1(a) only varied pedestrian size, in a plain crossing scenario. This variation covers both the static target and the pedestrian target, and applies to the newly introduced drive around scenario 4.2.5.2.18.

changes.new_text: In the extended test for the pedestrian target crossing into the path of the VUT during drive around manoeuvre (4.2.5.2.18.2), the test shall be executed at least with a pedestrian target moving at a different, but constant speed.
changes.reason: The wording repeats old 4.2.5.2.9.2.1(b), but the scope is the newly introduced drive around scenario 4.2.5.2.18, so it is a separate obligation.

changes.new_text: In the extended test for the pedestrian target crossing into the path of the VUT during drive around manoeuvre (4.2.5.2.18.2), the test shall be executed at least with a different angle of the pedestrian target path to the VUT path.
changes.reason: The wording repeats old 4.2.5.2.9.2.1(c), but the scope is the newly introduced drive around scenario 4.2.5.2.18, so it is a separate obligation.

changes.new_text: In the partially obstructed intersection scenario (VUT crossing the straight path of the vehicle target, Annex 4 / 4.2.5.2.19), the Base Test shall confirm the declared response capability of the system to recognize and offer right of way for a crossing vehicle target driving straight in an intersection.
changes.reason: The wording repeats old 4.2.5.2.14.1 (the unobstructed intersection Base Test), but the new paragraph sits under the newly introduced partially obstructed intersection scenario 4.2.5.2.19. It is therefore a separately applicable test obligation, not a renumbering of the old one. No base requirement (R-001 to R-117) covers it, so it is added.

changes.new_text: In the Base Test for the partially obstructed intersection (VUT crossing the straight path of a vehicle target), the VUT shall approach the impact point with another vehicle (passenger car or motorcycle) target in an initial straight line in an intersection from the near side direction only, to collide the side of the target vehicle at 25 per cent along the length of the target with the centre front of the VUT.
changes.reason: The paragraph sits under the new partially obstructed intersection scenario 4.2.5.2.19. It restricts the approach direction to the near side, whereas the old 4.2.5.2.14.1.1 (unobstructed crossing) allows either near side or far side. This is a separately scoped test setup obligation, not a renumbering. No base requirement R-### corresponds to it.

changes.new_text: In the Base Test for the partially obstructed intersection (VUT crossing the straight path of the vehicle target), the target shall approach at a speed of up to 60 km/h, depending on the declared system boundaries.
changes.reason: The parameter is the same as in the unobstructed intersection test (4.2.5.2.14.1.2). It is repeated here under the new partially obstructed intersection procedure (4.2.5.2.19), so it is a separately applicable test parameter.

changes.new_text: In the Base Test for the partially obstructed intersection (VUT crossing the straight path of the vehicle target), the VUT is expected to give right of way to the crossing target.
changes.reason: The expected outcome is the same as in the unobstructed intersection test (4.2.5.2.14.1.2). It is repeated here as a separate pass expectation under the new partially obstructed scenario (4.2.5.2.19).

changes.new_text: In the Base Test for the VUT crossing the straight path of a vehicle target in a partially obstructed intersection (Annex 4 / 4.2.5.2.19.1), a static target shall be placed in the opposite direction of travel at the same side of the intersection, such that it obstructs the view of the coming moving target but does not interfere with the path of the VUT.
changes.reason: The view-obstructing static target set-up is new and applies only to the newly introduced partially obstructed intersection scenario (4.2.5.2.19). No old clause sets up a static target that obstructs the view of a moving target in an intersection test, so the prior addition is supported.

changes.new_text: In the partially obstructed intersection scenario (VUT crossing the straight path of the vehicle target), the extended test shall demonstrate that the system is not unreasonably changing the control strategy for a crossing vehicle target driving straight in an intersection.
changes.reason: The wording repeats old 4.2.5.2.14.2, but that clause is scoped to the unobstructed intersection scenario. This one sits under new scenario 4.2.5.2.19 (partially obstructed intersection), so it is a separately scoped extended-test obligation and not a relocation. No old requirement in the base inventory covers it. R-116 and R-117 are general Appendix 4 control-strategy statements, not this scenario-specific test.

changes.new_text: In the extended testing for the partially obstructed intersection (VUT crossing the straight path of a vehicle target), the test shall be executed at least with different target vehicle types or categories.
changes.reason: Separately scoped extended-test variation for the new partially obstructed intersection scenario (4.2.5.2.19.2). The old 4.2.5.2.14.2.1(a) applies to the unobstructed intersection scenario only.

changes.new_text: In the extended testing for the partially obstructed intersection (VUT crossing the straight path of a vehicle target), the test shall be executed at least with different overlaps.
changes.reason: Independent variation item for the new partially obstructed intersection scenario. The old 4.2.5.2.14.2.1(b) is scoped to the unobstructed scenario.

changes.new_text: In the extended testing for the partially obstructed intersection (VUT crossing the straight path of a vehicle target), the test shall be executed at least with different lane positions of the VUT and the moving target vehicle.
changes.reason: Independent variation item for the new partially obstructed intersection scenario. The old 4.2.5.2.14.2.1(c) is scoped to the unobstructed scenario.

changes.new_text: In the extended testing for the partially obstructed intersection (VUT crossing the straight path of a vehicle target), the test shall be executed at least with different positions of the static target.
changes.reason: New variation item with no counterpart in the old unobstructed-intersection list. It relates to the static view-obstructing target introduced in 4.2.5.2.19.1.3.

changes.new_text: In the Base Test for the VUT turning across the path of an oncoming vehicle and cyclist, the test shall confirm the declared response capability of the system for an oncoming vehicle target while the VUT is turning in an intersection with multiple targets.
changes.reason: Paragraph 4.2.5.2.20.1 is a new test scenario (4.2.5.2.20, oncoming vehicle plus cyclist). The old 4.2.5.2.13.1 base test covered a single oncoming vehicle target with no cyclist. The multiple-target scope is a separate procedure obligation, even though the wording is largely repeated.

changes.new_text: In the Base Test for the VUT turning across the path of an oncoming vehicle and cyclist (multiple targets), the VUT shall approach the impact point with another vehicle (passenger car or motorcycle) target in an initial straight line followed by a turn in an intersection to cross the front edges of the target vehicle, with a lateral position giving a 50 per cent overlap of the width of the VUT.
changes.reason: The wording repeats the old oncoming-vehicle turning test (4.2.5.2.13.1.1), but it sits under the newly introduced multiple-target oncoming vehicle and cyclist test (4.2.5.2.20.1). That new procedure scope creates a separately applicable test obligation, and no base requirement represents it.

changes.new_text: In the Base Test for the VUT turning across the path of an oncoming vehicle and cyclist (multiple targets), the first target (the oncoming vehicle target) shall approach at a speed of up to 60 km/h.
changes.reason: The clause sits in a newly introduced multi-target scenario (4.2.5.2.20) and sets a speed limit for the first target. Similar wording in 4.2.5.2.14.1.2 / R-series Annex 4 clauses applies to different scenarios, and the new clause has no declared-system-boundaries qualifier. It is therefore a separately scoped new obligation.

changes.new_text: In the Base Test for the VUT turning across the path of an oncoming vehicle and cyclist (multiple targets), the cyclist target shall approach at 20 km/h +0/-0.4 km/h from a maximum of 1 m from the road edge.
changes.reason: New cyclist target speed, tolerance and start-position parameters for the multi-target turning scenario; no old clause has a cyclist target in this scenario.

changes.new_text: In the Base Test for the VUT turning across the path of an oncoming vehicle and cyclist (multiple targets), the cyclist target's positioning shall be coordinated with the moving target so that the cyclist target reaches the centreline of the road two seconds after the rear of the moving target passes the same virtual centreline.
changes.reason: Separate timing-coordination obligation between the cyclist and the moving vehicle target; no old counterpart exists in any scenario.

changes.new_text: In the Extended testing for the scenario in which the VUT turns across the path of an oncoming vehicle and cyclist (Annex 4, 4.2.5.2.20), the test shall demonstrate that the system is not unreasonably changing the control strategy for an oncoming vehicle target while the VUT is turning in an intersection.
changes.reason: Identical wording exists under the separate scenario 4.2.5.2.13.2 (oncoming vehicle turn, no cyclist). The new clause sits under the new 4.2.5.2.20 scenario (oncoming vehicle and cyclist, multiple targets), so it is a separately applicable extended-test obligation. It is not a relocation of the old one, and the old 4.2.5.2.13.2 remains in the new text. No equivalent R-ID exists, because R-116 and R-117 are general control-strategy requirements in Appendix 4 of Annex 3 and not scenario-specific extended test procedures.

changes.new_text: For the extended test in Annex 4, 4.2.5.2.20.2 (VUT turns across the path of an oncoming vehicle and cyclist; demonstrating that the system does not unreasonably change its control strategy for an oncoming vehicle target while the VUT is turning in an intersection), the test shall be executed at least with different target vehicle types or categories.
changes.reason: New scenario 4.2.5.2.20 (oncoming vehicle and cyclist). The same wording in the old 4.2.5.2.13.2.1(a) applies to a different scenario without a cyclist, so this is a separately scoped obligation.

changes.new_text: For the extended test in Annex 4, 4.2.5.2.20.2 (VUT turns across the path of an oncoming vehicle and cyclist), the test shall be executed at least with different overlaps.
changes.reason: Separately scoped test variation for the new oncoming vehicle and cyclist scenario. The old 'different overlaps' items belong to other scenarios (4.2.5.2.13 and 4.2.5.2.14).

changes.new_text: For the extended test in Annex 4, 4.2.5.2.20.2 (VUT turns across the path of an oncoming vehicle and cyclist), the test shall be executed at least with different lane positions of the vehicles and target.
changes.reason: Separately scoped test variation for the new scenario. The old lane-position items apply to other scenarios (4.2.5.2.13 and 4.2.5.2.14).
